categories.label: Architecture

signals.label: Circular dependencies between modules
signals.detail: 3 dependency cycle(s) prevent modules from being built, tested or replaced independently.

remediation.title: Break the dependency cycles
remediation.why: Cycles couple modules bidirectionally, so a change anywhere in the loop can break everything else in it.
remediation.how: Extract the shared contract into an interface owned by the lower layer, then invert the upward dependency.

signals.label: Layering violations
signals.detail: 8 dependenc(ies) point from a lower layer up into a higher one, inverting the intended flow.

remediation.title: Restore the layer boundaries
remediation.why: Upward dependencies make the lower layers un-reusable and drag presentation concerns into the domain.
remediation.how: Introduce an abstraction in the lower layer and inject the concrete implementation from the composition root.

signals.label: Hub components with excessive fan-in/out
signals.detail: 15 node(s) sit on a disproportionate number of relationships and act as change amplifiers.

remediation.title: Split the highest-traffic hubs
remediation.why: Every consumer of a hub is exposed to changes made for any other consumer.
remediation.how: Group the hub's members by the audience that uses them and publish narrow, role-specific interfaces.

signals.label: Densely connected module graph
signals.detail: Module dependency density is 24.6% - the recommended ceiling is 12%.

remediation.title: Reduce cross-module coupling
remediation.why: A dense graph means almost every module can be affected by almost every change.
remediation.how: Introduce a facade per bounded context and route cross-context traffic through it.

categories.label: Code Quality

signals.label: Functions above the complexity threshold
signals.detail: 7 of 360 functions (2%) exceed a cyclomatic complexity of 10.

remediation.title: Decompose the 7 most complex functions
remediation.why: Every extra branch multiplies the paths a reader and a test must cover.
remediation.how: Extract guard clauses and cohesive blocks into named helpers, then cover each with a focused test.

signals.label: Functions with long parameter lists
signals.detail: 5 function(s) take six or more parameters, which usually hides a missing value object.

signals.label: Oversized source files
signals.detail: 0 file(s) exceed 1000 lines and 1 exceed 600 lines.

remediation.title: Split the largest source files
remediation.why: Large files hide multiple responsibilities and make every merge a conflict.
remediation.how: Move each cohesive group of functions into its own module and re-export a narrow public surface.

categories.summary: Technical Debt needs attention. The largest deduction is "High maintainability defects" (-24.0 pts) and 2 further issues.

quick_wins.title: Remediate the 1 high security finding(s)
quick_wins.why: These algorithms are collision-prone or trivially reversible and are unacceptable for secrets or integrity.
quick_wins.how: Use SHA-256/SHA-3 for digests, bcrypt/argon2 for passwords and AES-GCM for symmetric encryption.

quick_wins.title: Document the public API surface
quick_wins.why: Undocumented public symbols force every consumer to read the implementation to learn the contract.
quick_wins.how: Add a one-paragraph doc comment stating purpose, parameters, return value and failure modes.

quick_wins.title: Add a CI pipeline that runs the suite
quick_wins.why: Tests that are not run automatically stop being run at all.
quick_wins.how: Add a workflow that installs dependencies and runs the test command on every push and pull request.

quick_wins.title: Stop swallowing errors
quick_wins.why: Errors disappear without a trace, so failures surface later as corrupt data instead of an alert.
quick_wins.how: Log the error with context, or let it propagate to a handler that can decide what to do.

quick_wins.title: Index the foreign key columns
quick_wins.why: Unindexed foreign keys turn every join and cascading delete into a table scan.
quick_wins.how: Add an index on each foreign key column and verify with the query planner.

medium_term.title: Restore the layer boundaries
medium_term.why: Upward dependencies make the lower layers un-reusable and drag presentation concerns into the domain.
medium_term.how: Introduce an abstraction in the lower layer and inject the concrete implementation from the composition root.

medium_term.title: Expand test coverage on the least-covered modules
medium_term.why: Modules with no tests are the ones where defects survive the longest.
medium_term.how: Add characterisation tests to the untested modules listed in the evidence, starting with the busiest.

medium_term.title: Break the dependency cycles
medium_term.why: Cycles couple modules bidirectionally, so a change anywhere in the loop can break everything else in it.
medium_term.how: Extract the shared contract into an interface owned by the lower layer, then invert the upward dependency.

medium_term.title: Fix the 6 high-impact performance issue(s)
medium_term.why: One query per row multiplies latency by the size of the collection.
medium_term.how: Fetch the rows in a single query with a join, an IN clause or an eager-loading option.

medium_term.title: Decompose the 7 most complex functions
medium_term.why: Every extra branch multiplies the paths a reader and a test must cover.
medium_term.how: Extract guard clauses and cohesive blocks into named helpers, then cover each with a focused test.

medium_term.title: Split the largest source files
medium_term.why: Large files hide multiple responsibilities and make every merge a conflict.
medium_term.how: Move each cohesive group of functions into its own module and re-export a narrow public surface.

long_term.title: Reduce cross-module coupling
long_term.why: A dense graph means almost every module can be affected by almost every change.
long_term.how: Introduce a facade per bounded context and route cross-context traffic through it.

long_term.title: Split the highest-traffic hubs
long_term.why: Every consumer of a hub is exposed to changes made for any other consumer.
long_term.how: Group the hub's members by the audience that uses them and publish narrow, role-specific interfaces.

long_term.title: Split the god classes by responsibility
long_term.why: A type that does everything cannot be understood, tested or changed in isolation.
long_term.how: Group the methods by the data they touch and extract each group into a collaborator with a single reason to change.
